items.title: Detect self-host worktree and runtime realpath mismatch
items.context: Bind the invoked CLI runtime realpath, repository root, git worktree root, and current command authority. A worktree invocation whose global runtime resolves into the main workspace must be classified before story-scoped mutation; normal external consumer repositories and correctly local runtimes must remain valid.

happy.desc: In a self-host story worktree, canonicalize the invoked CLI runtime realpath, repository root, git worktree root, and git common-dir; classify a runtime resolving into the main checkout as a mismatch before any story-scoped mutation.
A worktree-local node bin/lattice.js runtime whose canonical realpath belongs to the active worktree is accepted and reaches normal command dispatch.

edge.desc: Classification is identical when the executable, repository path, or worktree path is reached through symlinks, and when .git is a worktree file pointing at a shared common-dir.
An ordinary external consumer repository using a global Lattice installation is not rejected as a self-host mismatch; its existing advisory behavior remains intact.
Within a self-host worktree, the narrowly documented global-fallback exception permits read-only session_brief only; other commands remain subject to runtime authority classification.

adversarial.desc: Nested cwd, path aliases, dot-segments, and symlinked global launchers cannot make a main-checkout runtime appear worktree-local or bypass the mismatch decision.
Missing or malformed git worktree/common-dir metadata fails closed for story-scoped mutation without misclassifying a normal external repository as Proofbound self-hosting.

items.userSees: User sees "Runtime authority check: PASS — active CLI resolves inside the current story worktree." before any handler executes.

verificationEvidence.note: Hermetic linked-worktree fixture canonicalizes runtime, project, worktree, main, and common-dir identities and blocks the main-checkout runtime.
Worktree-local bin/lattice.js identity is classified PASS.
Symlink launcher, dot-segment project path, and linked-worktree git metadata resolve to the same canonical mismatch.
Non-self external git consumer remains executable and advisory.
Only session_brief with explicit LATTICE_CODEX_ENTRYPOINT=global-fallback is exempt; validate stays blocked.
Canonical realpath and git identities defeat nested aliases, dot segments, and symlink spelling.
Unresolved runtime identity is fail-closed when authoritative runtime is required, while external consumers bypass self-host classification.

items.title: Fail fast with one canonical local-entrypoint recovery command
items.context: Return a stable reason code and an actionable node bin/lattice.js command before expensive validation or lifecycle work starts. The diagnostic must distinguish stale global runtime from ordinary missing build, wrong cwd, or external-project advisory cases.

happy.desc: A stale-global self-host invocation fails before expensive or mutating work with one stable machine-readable reason code and one copyable worktree-local node bin/lattice.js recovery command.
Running the emitted recovery command with the same original command and arguments executes through the current worktree runtime and proceeds normally.

edge.desc: Diagnostics distinguish stale-global-runtime mismatch from missing local build, wrong cwd, and external-consumer advisory cases, with a specific next action for each.
Repeated identical mismatches return the same reason code and canonical recovery command independent of symlink spelling, cwd spelling, or terminal session.
Global-fallback guidance is offered only for read-only session_brief recovery; it never recommends a global entrypoint for validation, lifecycle, review, or other mutating/expensive commands.

adversarial.desc: The rejection path records zero mutating-handler invocations and starts zero validation/dispatch subprocesses before returning the diagnostic.

Command names or arguments containing spaces, quotes, JSON, or shell metacharacters are rendered as a safe, semantically identical recovery command rather than truncated or executable diagnostic text.

items.userSees: Blocked [stale_global_runtime_in_worktree] before dispatch. Loaded runtime belongs to the main checkout. Retry: node bin/lattice.js <same command and arguments>

verificationEvidence.note: CLI choke point rejects stale main runtime before Store, registry, hooks, handler dispatch, or validation and emits stable reasonCode plus one recovery command.
The emitted worktree-local entrypoint form loads the current build and reaches normal command dispatch.
Stale mismatch has a stable code; bootstrap retains distinct missing-build recovery; ordinary cwd/lifecycle errors remain downstream diagnostics.
Canonical identities produce the same reason and deterministic recovery command across symlink and path aliases.
Global fallback is documented as one exact session_brief heartbeat command, never a generic command placeholder.
Authority gate is mechanically located before Store/registry creation and therefore before hooks, handlers, validation subprocesses, and persistence.
Shell quoting preserves JSON, spaces, semicolons, and metacharacters as one inert argument in the recovery command.

items.title: Prove stale-global rejection and correct-local execution end to end
items.context: Use hermetic main-plus-worktree fixtures to reproduce the B-914f failure: global runtime points at main old dist while worktree has newer behavior. Assert zero mutating handler execution on rejection, successful worktree-local execution, no regression for external projects, and runtime fact/doctor contract coverage.

happy.desc: A hermetic main-plus-story-worktree fixture reproduces B-914f: the global launcher resolves to an older main dist, is rejected immediately, and the emitted worktree-local command executes the newer behavior successfully.
The end-to-end proof asserts the stale-global rejection reason, canonical recovery command, worktree-local success result, and zero handler/validation execution on the rejected attempt.

edge.desc: Hermetic cases cover direct paths, symlinked launchers, linked-worktree .git/common-dir resolution, nested cwd, correctly local runtime, read-only session_brief global fallback, and a non-self-host external consumer.

Doctor and runtime-fact contract checks expose the canonical entrypoint/global realpath/project-local bin facts without moving them into the process-fact registry or hard-failing external-reference advisories.

adversarial.desc: Instrument the dispatch boundary so rejection proves pre-dispatch zero handler invocation, zero evidence/story mutation, and zero spawned expensive command even if the requested command is validate or story_advance.
A stale global runtime cannot pass by spoofing argv[0], PATH order, cwd text, repository basename, or symlink aliases; authority is derived from canonical filesystem and git identities.
A correctly local runtime and an external consumer remain executable under the same harness, preventing a universal global-runtime ban from satisfying the negative tests.

items.userSees: User sees "Runtime entrypoint authority smoke: PASS — stale global calls executed 0 handlers; local and external controls passed."

verificationEvidence.note: Hermetic copied runtime records main-old and worktree-new builds, rejects the main CLI, then executes the emitted worktree-local recovery command successfully.
E2E asserts stable reason, canonical Retry command, recovered JSON result, hook absent, validation marker absent, and no .lattice state on rejection.
Harness covers direct and symlink launchers, linked .git/common-dir, nested cwd, local runtime, explicit session_brief fallback, and external consumer CLI.
Doctor/runtime registry contract verifies entrypoint-authority as runtime-only alongside canonical entrypoint, global realpath, and local-bin facts.
A stale validate request proves zero preCommand hook, zero validation subprocess, and zero evidence/runtime state before rejection.
Canonical loaded-module git root defeats symlink launcher, PATH preference, nested cwd, argv worktree spoof, dot segments, and aliases.
Correct local runtime and external consumer controls execute under the same harness; validation protocol retains external advisory behavior and runtime fact shape.
